clips.asr_text: Today's topic is The Open Window.
Framton Nuttel has come to the country to rest, but visiting a stranger's home makes him uneasy. What will happen during this visit, and how will he respond?
Listen for what the girl tells Framton about the open window.
The girl says her aunt's husband and brothers never came back from a shooting trip. What will Frampton think when the aunt comes in and talks about the open window?
The girl says the men never came back, but her aunt says they will return soon. What will Frampton see when he turns toward the window?
Letter of Introduction
A letter that introduces someone to another person.
a most peculiar visitor.
A very unusual person who comes to visit.
Take turns.
To do something one after another, with each person having a chance.

The drawing-room was quiet, but Framton Nuttel could not relax. He turned his letter of introduction between his fingers. His doctor had ordered peace and quiet in the country, not visits to strangers.
My aunt will be down soon.
said the fifteen-year-old girl opposite him.
Do you know much about her?
Nothing, really?
Her eyes moved to the French window, open to the lawn.
You may wonder why that's open in October.
It's quite warm.
Frampton said.
Three years ago today, her husband and her two young brothers went shooting. They left through that window.
She paused, and Frampton waited.
They never came back. They crossed the marsh where the ground seemed firm, and all three sank into a bog. Their little brown spaniel went too. The bodies were never found.
The letter lay still in Crampton's hands.

My aunt thinks they'll return. She keeps the window open until dark. Her husband had his white waterproof coat over his shoulders. Her youngest brother sang, Oh brother, why do you bound? He always did that to annoy her.
The girl swallowed.
Sometimes when it starts getting dark, I almost feel they really will.
The door opened. His hostess hurried in, full of apologies.
I hope my niece has entertained you. You don't mind the open window? My husband and brothers will be back directly. They've been shooting. Such a mess they'll make of my carpets.
Frampton struggled to find a safe subject. He explained that his doctor had ordered complete rest and no excitement. She listened but kept looking past him towards the lawn. Then her face brightened.
Here they are at last!
The girl stared at the window, her lips parted. A cold feeling spread through Crampton as he turned.
Three men were approaching, across the darkening lawn, carrying guns. One had a white coat over his shoulders. A tired brown spaniel followed them. A young voice called through the twilight.
Oh brother, why do you bound?
Frampton grabbed his hat and stick. He rushed through the hall and out of the gate, forcing a passing cyclist into the hedge. The men stepped through the window.
Who is that running away?
asked the husband, wiping his muddy boots.
A most peculiar visitor.
His wife said,
You'd think he'd seen a ghost!
It was the spaniel.
the girl said calmly.
He told me he was terrified of dogs. A pack once chased him into a cemetery. He spent the night in an empty grave with them looking down at him.
She glanced at the sleepy dog.
He said they took turns.
